title: In vitro characterization of [<sup>3</sup>H]VAT in cells, animal and human brain tissues for vesicular acetylcholine transporter.
abstract: Vesicular acetylcholine transporter plays a crucial role in the cholinergic system, and its alterations is implicated in several neurodegenerative disorders. We recently developed a PET imaging tracer [<sup>18</sup>F]VAT to target VAChT in vivo with high affinity and selectivity. Here we report in vitro characterization of [<sup>3</sup>H]VAT, a tritiated counterpart of [<sup>18</sup>F]VAT. Using human VAChT-rich cell membrane extracts, a saturated binding curve was obtained for [<sup>3</sup>H]VAT with K<sub>d</sub> = 6.5 nM and B<sub>max</sub> = 22.89 pmol/mg protein. In the [<sup>3</sup>H]VAT competition-binding assay with a panel of CNS ligands, binding inhibition of [<sup>3</sup>H]VAT was observed using VAChT ligands, the K<sub>i</sub> values ranged from 5.41 to 33.3 nM. No inhibition was detected using a panel of other CNS ligands. In vitro [<sup>3</sup>H]VAT autoradiography of rat brain sections showed strong signals in the striatum, moderate to high signals in vermis, thalamus, cortex, and hippocampus, and weak signals in cerebellum. Strong [<sup>3</sup>H]VAT ARG signals were also observed from striatal sections of normal nonhuman primates and human brains. Competitive ARG study with human striatal sections demonstrated strong ARG signals of [<sup>3</sup>H]VAT in caudate and putamen were blocked significantly by either VAChT ligand TZ659 or (-)-vesamicol, but not by the σ<sub>1</sub> receptor ligand Yun-122. ARG study also indicated that signal in the striatal sections from PSP human brains was lower than normal human brains. These data provide solid evidence supporting [<sup>18</sup>F]VAT as a suitable PET radiotracer for quantitative assessment of VAChT levels in vivo.
